name: Traveller Danish
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Miskow, Johan & Viggo Brondal 1923. Sigojnersprog i Danmark (cited on Glottolog trav1237; Brondal's description plausibly notes accentuation); not found online

new_statements.quote: Noget selvstændigt og konsekvent Lydsystem er aabenbart ikke længer tilstede. Saa vidt man af Optegnelsens Lydgengivelse kan slutte, bruges væsentlig de danske eller tyske Lyd; [...] En Tilbøjelighed til at svække alle ubetonede Vokaler til e [ə], skyldes tydeligt dansk Indflydelse. [p. 134] — jandéli, Pibe (Tryk paa 2. Stavelse. DSt. 1909, 117 jandéla). [p. 115] — kommora, Stue. („Trykket paa første Stavelse". [...]) [p. 119] — transori, Tallerken. (Tryk paa 2. Stavelse). [p. 133]
new_statements.translation: No independent and consistent sound system is evidently present any longer. As far as one can conclude from the transcription of the notes, essentially the Danish or German sounds are used; [...] A tendency to weaken all unstressed vowels to e [ə] is clearly due to Danish influence. — jandéli 'pipe' (stress on the 2nd syllable). — kommora 'room' ("stress on the first syllable"). — transori 'plate' (stress on the 2nd syllable).
new_statements.citation: Miskow, Johan & Viggo Brøndal. 1923. Sigøjnersprog i Danmark. Danske Studier 1923: 97-145.
new_statements.locator: p. 134 (concluding remarks after the wordlist); entry-level stress notes at pp. 115 (jandéli), 119 (kommora), 133 (transori)
new_statements.rule_in_words: No general rule is stated anywhere. Brøndal's only phonological summary says the register has no sound system of its own and uses Danish/German sounds, with reduction of unstressed vowels to schwa under Danish influence. Stress is recorded word by word in Miskow's notes: initial in kommora, second-syllable in jandéli and transori (both loans); stød ('Stødtone') is noted on the monosyllables khil and prral. Prince 1925: 100 adds that the (par)oxytone accent of kommora was probably influenced by German Kammer.
new_statements.exceptions: None as such; the authors stress that the material is unsystematic ('there is no longer any norm', p. 135) and that the informants themselves vary.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation-form wordlist of a moribund Romani-lexicon cryptolect ('Romnisk') collected over c. 20 years from Danish 'Rejsende' (Sindi) families who otherwise spoke Low/High German; no phrase-level prosody.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog trav1237 (ISO rmd 'Traveller Danish', alt. names Rodi, Rotwelsch) covers two different things. (a) The Romani-lexicon cryptolect ('Romnisk', speakers self-named Sindi/Romani) of the Danish 'Rejsende' (grinder, circus and musician families), documented by Miskow 1904, 1909, Miskow & Brøndal 1923 and Prince 1925: a Scandoromani-type para-Romani register on a Low/High German and Danish base; the statement above is about this variety. (b) The Germanic-based Jutlandic rotvælsk / kjæltringsprog of the natmandsfolk, documented by Dorph 1824/1837, Dyrlund 1872 and H. P. Hansen 1917/1922; Brøndal 1923: 135-136 states explicitly that the two are unrelated ('Det ægte romaniske har principielt intet med Rotvælsk at gøre'). No separate glottocode for Danish rotvælsk is known to me; the Norwegian counterpart of (a) is trav1236 (Traveller Norwegian).

sources.note: No general stress rule. Wordlist entries carry stress notes from Miskow's field notes: jandéli 'pipe' "(Tryk paa 2. Stavelse...)" p. 115; kommora 'room' "(„Trykket paa første Stavelse"...)" p. 119; transori 'plate' "(Tryk paa 2. Stavelse)" p. 133; khil 'butter' (p. 118) and prral 'brother' (p. 125) "„med Stødtone"". Concluding remarks p. 134: no independent, consistent sound system survives; essentially Danish or German sounds are used; a tendency to weaken all unstressed vowels to [ə] is due to Danish influence. Pp. 135-136 state that this Romani register has nothing to do with the Jutlandic…

sources.citation: Dyrlund, F[olmer]. 1872. Tatere og Natmandsfolk i Danmark. København: Gyldendal.
sources.note: Historical monograph with a long analysis of Dorph's rotvælsk lexicon (the Germanic-based kjæltringsprog, not the Romani register). Incidental accent notes only: note 22 (p. c. 342) "Ægte sigensk er tonefaldet i *gabén" (the accent in gabén is genuinely Gypsy); p. c. 335 hœnafirusk "(tonen på sidste stavelse)". No general rule.
